findings.title: Provider-tier PII filter ignores platform-aware exclusion
findings.description: HttpProvider::apply_outbound_safety gates the per-text-block PII filter on is_provider_excluded (global) only and calls engine.filter() (also global, no platform). It does NOT consult is_platform_excluded nor receive a platform name. Operators with [platform_policies.X].exclude_providers bypassed at runtime_guard are surprised at http_provider re-applying PII filtering on the unredacted payload. Same gap also downgrades per-platform PII action overrides (e.g. platform_policies.X.phone = warn).
findings.suggested_fix: Propagate platform name through execute/apply_outbound_safety and call is_platform_excluded(platform, provider) + filter_with_platform; OR remove the second-tier PII filter from apply_outbound_safety on the grounds that the guardrail pipeline already covers it.

findings.title: PiiEngine::reload lacks the partial-load summary warning emitted by new
findings.description: PiiEngine::new computes configured_custom - loaded_custom and emits one operator-facing warn! summarising partial custom-rule load. PiiEngine::reload does not — it calls the same build_rules but skips the summary. Hot-reload of a half-broken config yields per-rule warns but no top-level signal. Asymmetric operational story between boot and reload.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the same configured_custom / loaded_custom logic in reload (extract into a helper), or drop it from both.

findings.title: FilterResult.skipped_count is computed but never read
findings.description: skipped_count is set in filter_with_config whenever a Block action cannot be applied because matched offsets fall off a char boundary / outside the (mutated) text. The doc-comment explicitly says the audit pipeline (runtime_guard) can use this as a triage signal. Grep across src/ and tests/ finds zero non-test readers — runtime_guard::apply_filter_result only reads blocked_count and warned_count. The field is permanently zero-valued for any consumer.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire apply_filter_result to escalate skipped_count > 0 to a Critical audit entry (the original intent) and document the convention, or drop the field.

findings.title: PII allowlist has no direct unit tests
findings.description: src/pii/allowlist.rs ships with zero #[cfg(test)] mod tests. All coverage reaches is_allowed indirectly via engine integration tests. The static sets (TEST_PHONES, LOCAL_IPS) and the regexes (SYSTEM_EMAIL_PATTERNS — pattern widened previously by 56a84247e/c59090033 for the case-fold in both directions) are exactly where a regression in pattern semantics would land first.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a #[cfg(test)] mod with positive tests for each rule-name branch (phone, email, ip_address), a negative test for an unrelated rule (api_key returns false for everything), and a case-fold test for the email branch covering .example, .EXAMPLE, noreply@, NO-REPLY@.

findings.title: dedup_overlapping is O(n²)
findings.description: dedup_overlapping uses result.iter().any(|existing| m.start < existing.end && m.end > existing.start) inside a loop over the input. For typical outbound PII (1–3 matches per message) this is invisible, but the path is on the hot outbound pipeline and the surrounding filter_with_config is invoked once per outbound text block. A pathological case — a long string with many adjacent rule hits, e.g. a 1-MB CSV column with many credit-card Luhn-valid numbers — would walk Vec<PiiMatch> quadratically.
findings.suggested_fix: Sort spans by (start, -end) first and run a sweep, or bucket by start/16 and check only the small bucket — either removes the quadratic worst-case while preserving semantics.

findings.title: Double PII filter with divergent semantics (filter_with_platform vs filter)
findings.description: runtime_guard::process_outbound calls filter_with_platform (platform-aware); the request then continues to HttpProvider::apply_outbound_safety which calls engine.filter (global-config, no platform). The two paths use different filter functions whose semantics diverge whenever [platform_policies.X] overrides the global config. When runtime_guard elects to redact, http_provider tier is a no-op. When runtime_guard elects to skip (platform exclusion), http_provider tier may still redact. Same root cause as PII-001 framed as duplication.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the PII block from apply_outbound_safety on the grounds that the guardrail layer already covers it; OR propagate platform name to apply_outbound_safety and gate on is_platform_excluded(None, &self.name) so the second tier does not contradict the first.

findings.title: effective_config clones PrivacyConfig on three early-return paths
findings.description: effective_config has three early-return branches — no platform, no platform policy, policy with all-None fields — each returning self.config.clone(). With pii_filtering: true, seven PiiAction defaults, and a few Vecs/HashMaps in PrivacyConfig, each clone is a one-shot allocation per filter call. Hot path, easily avoidable.
findings.suggested_fix: Return a thin enum (e.g. EffectiveConfig<'a> { Global(&'a PrivacyConfig), Owned(PrivacyConfig) }) and match in filter_with_config, or split into effective_config_owned and a borrowing version for the identity cases.

findings.title: Bearer-token char class misses +/= (base64 padding)
findings.description: The Bearer branch (?i:Bearer)\s+[a-zA-Z0-9._\-]{20,} accepts alphanumerics plus ., _, -. Standard base64 alphabet also includes +, /, =. A Bearer <token> containing those characters is not matched by ApiKeyRule. runtime_guard's ExecLeakDetector covers this with a broader bearer_token rule (per src/exec/leak_detector.rs:239-260), but the PII module's stand-alone capability is documented as filters-outbound — a leaky Bearer in a context where only the PII module ran would slip through.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the bearer token char class to [a-zA-Z0-9._\-+/=]{20,} or add an explicit \+ branch. Add a regression test asserting that Bearer abc+def/ghi= is detected by the PII rule alone.

findings.title: init and reload build different lookup tables (duplicated code)
findings.description: PiiEngine::new and PiiEngine::reload both rebuild custom_rule_actions and excluded_providers, but the constructions are open-coded in two places (not extracted into a helper). If a future field is added (e.g. effective_providers or a fast-path phone_digit_set), the same code must be edited in three places (new, reload, and the effective_config indexing path). Drift is a likely failure mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract fn lookup_tables(config: &PrivacyConfig) -> (HashMap<String, PiiAction>, HashSet<String>) and call it from both new and reload.

non_findings_verified: PiiAllowlist is wired into filter_with_config (engine.rs:319); not decorative.
Custom rule safety via bounded_builder (security/safe_regex.rs); no compile-time memory blowup.
Rule registration parity: 7 built-in names appear in both build_rules and action_for_rule.
ssh_key.rs header pattern no longer carries a back-reference; SSH key pairing in detect is plain Rust.
Severity/blocks ordering in dedup_fixed; covered by test_overlap_block_wins_over_higher_severity_warn.
Case-fold in email/allowlist tested both directions (56a84247e).
RwLock discipline consistent; poison-safe recovery via unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).
Char-boundary safety on UTF-8 (engine.rs:378-379 + phone.rs is_timestamp_context snap).
Warn action preserves text (engine.rs:391-405) — caller-visible Warn semantics correct.
